newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan carrier says Cambodia route on schedule.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan carrier says Cambodia route on schedule.

text.p: Taiwan's EVA Airways said on Wednesday its inaugural flight to Cambodia would take of on April 10, fixing a date despite protests from rival China.
"Our plan for direct non-stop flights to Cambodia has not changed. The airline will dispatch a 212-seat Boeing 767-200 to Phnom Penh on April 10," an EVA spokesman told Reuters.

He said EVA, a unit of shipping giant Evergreen Marine, has received no government notice asking it to stop the new service despite Taipei media reports that cast doubt on the existence of an enabling bilateral aviation pact.
EVA announced the Taipei-Phnom Penh service in February, saying Taiwan had signed a direct air link agreement with Cambodia in December.
Reports of the accord angered China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province unqualified to enter into sovereign agreements with other countries.
Taiwan media on Wednesday quoted Prak Sokhon, a senior adviser to Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, as saying Phnom Penh was unaware of any Taiwan-Cambodia accord.
Beijing has said it was firmly opposed to countries with which it has diplomatic relations establishing official air links with Taiwan.
China, which has sought to retake Taiwan since a civil war split them in 1949, insists that states get Beijing's blessing before starting non-governmental air links with the island.
Cambodia recognises China diplomatically and has no official ties with Taiwan.
Taiwan aviation officials on Wednesday insisted the deal took effect on December 18 immediately after it was signed.
They said Cambodia faced tremendous pressure from China and understood that some Cambodian officials might have disavowed the agreement, the state-funded Central News Agency reported.
"Currently there is no change" in the agreement, the agency quoted an unnamed civil aviation official as saying.
EVA senior vice president K.T. Chiu issued a statement saying he believed the route would be profitable, given the rapid increase in the number of Taiwan visitors to Cambodia.
Statistics show 4,480 of Cambodia's 35,329 visitors in 1996 were from Taiwan, more than from anywhere else.
Cambodia approved US$80 million worth of investment from Taiwan in 1996, compared with US$18 million in 1995.
